page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The open window
title: The open window
description:
How do you explain if there's been a mix-up? Paul, the boss, leaves a message. He wants ideas for a new marketing strategy for their new laser-curved fruit range. Anna gets straight down to work but when Paul turns up, Tom gets all the credit. There's a big mix-up and it's time for Anna to learn some language that explains there has been a misunderstanding.
This episode focuses on politely saying there has been a misunderstanding.
phrases: I think there's been a misunderstanding.
There's been a bit of a mix-up.

listening_challenge.question: Tom found one of his certificates on the floor. What was it for?
listening_challenge.answer: Plastic Pear Salesman of the Year

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello, it's a chilly start to the day at Tip Top Trading.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hi Denise!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Good morning Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Brrr... it's so cold in here.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: The window was left open overnight.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: My papers have been blown everywhere.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Mine too! Tom was the last one here last night – it must've been him who left the window open.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Brrr.... Right then, to work! Oh, there's a note from Paul, it must've fallen off my desk: 'I would like your ideas on our stock management system for our new laser-curve fruit range, so we know we can keep up with demand. Please write me a couple of pages of suggestions and leave it on my desk. I'll be back this afternoon.' Wow! I have to come up with ideas for a stock management system! Gosh, where do I begin?!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Good morning.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Morning!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Hey, my certificate for Plastic Pear Salesman of the Year is on the floor!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right... stock management systems... stock-up on your laser-curved lemons … My first idea is to calculate the total….

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, Anna has finished her report and left it on Paul's desk, but things aren't that simple. Er, Anna, there's going to be a problem.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh? A problem, bbbbut…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Let me teach you some phrases you might need to explain that there's been a mistake:
I think there's been a misunderstanding.
Or:
There's been a bit of a mix-up.
Anna: But what misunderstanding? What mix-up?
Narrator: You could also use:
Let me explain what happened...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But-

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Ah, good afternoon everyone.

transcript.speaker: All
transcript.text: Hello.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Tom, this is an excellent piece of work!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Sorry?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: These are by far the best ideas you've ever had.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I don't understand.
PaulOur stock management system!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Can I see? … Oh, that's not mine.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Eh?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I think there's been a misunderstanding. I did it.

transcript.speaker: Paul & Tom
transcript.text: You?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I got your note Paul, here.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: No, no, that note was for Tom.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, then there's been a bit of a mix-up.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Did you take that note from my desk?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No, no!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I suppose you threw my pear salesman certificate on the floor at the same time too!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I didn’t! Let me explain. The wind must have blown the note for Tom under my desk.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Tom left the window open overnight. Our papers were blown all over the place.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I see, well, golly gosh. In that case, well done, Anna! Excellent work, even though you weren't meant to do it. And Tom, your ideas are still welcome of course. Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Sorry Tom.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What? Oh, I'm not bothered. I've still got some great ideas in my head anyway.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yeah, right! Let's leave Tom to get on with his 'great ideas' and listen again those phrases Anna used to explain the misunderstanding:
Well, the mix-up gave Anna a chance to shine – Paul certainly seemed impressed with her work. Maybe it will bring her new opportunities. Until next time, bye!
